register.name: Horn of Africa Initiative: Djibouti Regional Economic Corridor
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant · Additional financing approved 18 June 2026
register.text: US$45 million of additional financing, an IDA grant, for transport, logistics and road safety on the Djibouti to Addis Ababa southern corridor, which brings total World Bank financing for the project to US$205 million. It widens high-risk sections of National Road 1 between Arta and Doudoubala into a dual carriageway and adds roadside rest areas and marketplaces, with at least half of the stalls for women; more than 250,000 people are to gain access to more resilient roads by 2033, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Djibouti Economic Diversification Program
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant · Program-for-Results · Approved 27 March 2026
register.text: An IDA grant of US$25.75 million, the country’s first Program-for-Results financing and the first operation in the region co-led by the World Bank and IFC, within a total envelope of US$75.75 million for 2026 to 2034. It supports the governance of state-owned enterprises and access to public procurement, the business and investment climate, and the competitiveness of small and medium enterprises, including their access to finance, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Groundwater Resilience and Water Supply Project (DJIRESA)
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant · Approved 16 March 2026
register.text: A US$35 million World Bank grant to build and rehabilitate rural water systems, professionalise their operation and maintenance, and set up a national groundwater information system. It is expected to give reliable basic water services to 127,000 people in rural areas and to strengthen climate resilience for at least 167,000 people, which serves the water standard.
register.note: 127,000 people to gain reliable basic water services

register.name: Expanding Opportunities for Learning Project, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 7 May 2025 · IDA grant $6.5M · Global Partnership for Education grant $4.85M
register.text: Additional financing of US$11.35 million, made of a US$6.5 million IDA grant and a US$4.85 million grant from the Global Partnership for Education, which brings total project financing to US$41.7 million. It widens access to basic education, lays the groundwork for quality preschool and strengthens teaching, with a focus on refugees, rural children, girls and children with special needs; it serves the education standard.

register.name: Integrated Community Resilience Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 14 March 2025 · includes $9M from the IDA Window for Host Communities and Refugees
register.text: A World Bank project of US$31 million, including US$9 million from IDA’s Window for Host Communities and Refugees, to improve basic infrastructure and services, strengthen social safety nets and widen economic opportunities for vulnerable communities. It targets the Dikhil region and the refugee-hosting regions of Obock and Ali Sabieh, and serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Economic and Financial Governance Project
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant · Approved 16 January 2025
register.text: An IDA grant of US$20 million to make tax collection more efficient, make public spending more transparent and give citizens easier access to online government services. Stronger revenue and spending systems are the base from which a state finances the seven standards.
register.note: Tax, public spending and online public services

register.name: Roads, urban adaptation and food systems
register.detail: African Development Fund and Green Climate Fund · Signed 5 February 2026 · ADF grants $22M and $30M · GCF grant $14M and loan $14M
register.text: Four agreements with the African Development Bank Group: a US$22 million ADF grant to rehabilitate seven kilometres of urban roads in Djibouti city, a US$30 million ADF grant for a key road axis of the Djibouti–Ethiopia–South Sudan Regional Transport Corridor, and a US$14 million grant and a US$14 million loan from the Green Climate Fund under the Building Resilience around Food and Livelihoods (BREFOL) programme. BREFOL serves the food and livelihood standards.
register.note: Includes $28 million from the Green Climate Fund

register.name: National Oncology Center
register.detail: Islamic Development Bank · Signed 3 February 2026 · Jeddah · total project cost $28.35M
register.text: A US$26.10 million financing agreement with the Islamic Development Bank to establish Djibouti’s first National Oncology Center, in a project of US$28.35 million. The centre is expected to provide outpatient cancer services to 6,000 people and inpatient services to 1,200 people each year, which serves the health standard.

register.name: Djibouti City sanitation networks, five neighbourhoods (PERRAD)
register.detail: AFD and European Union · Works launched 16 June 2025 · ONEAD · neighbourhoods 5, 6, 7, 7-bis and Cité Stade
register.text: The Djibouti City Sanitation Networks Extension and Rehabilitation Project, co-financed by AFD and the European Union with the national water and sanitation office ONEAD as owner and operator, launched work on about twenty kilometres of collective sewers in five neighbourhoods and inaugurated a second wastewater treatment plant at Douda. Nearly 30,000 people are to gain access to the collective sanitation service, which serves the shelter standard, measured on this page by safely managed sanitation.
register.note: Total budget for the sewer works; the AFD and EU shares are not stated

register.name: Health system reform support (Parss)
register.text: A €7 million AFD grant for the project to support reform of the health system, which backs Djibouti’s health strategy. The quality of care in six public polyclinics is to be strengthened, with the steering, regulation and planning capacity of the Ministry of Health; it serves the health standard.
register.note: Quality of care in six public polyclinics

register.name: Energy efficiency in administrative buildings (Peeba)
register.text: A €7 million AFD grant to cut energy use in about ten administrative buildings, with works such as roof insulation and solar panels, and a revolving fund so that the project can be replicated. It serves the energy standard.
register.note: About ten public buildings and a revolving fund

register.name: Performance of the water service of ONEAD (Prospero)
register.detail: AFD · grant · Signed October 2022 · with €5M of EU funds delegated to AFD
register.text: A €10 million AFD grant, with €5 million of European Union funds delegated to AFD, to improve the performance and operating conditions of the water service of ONEAD, the national water and sanitation office. A stronger utility serves the water standard.

register.name: Ghoubet wind farm, 60 MW (Red Sea Power)
register.detail: FMO · senior secured loan · effective 21 December 2022 · refinancing
register.text: An FMO senior secured loan of US$16.67 million to Red Sea Power to refinance the wind farm of about 60 MW at Ghoubet, with a 220 MVA substation and a five-kilometre overhead line. The developers are FMO Private Equity, Climate Investor One, Africa Finance Corporation and Great Horn Investment Holdings; wind power serves the energy standard.
register.note: Refinances the wind farm at Ghoubet

register.name: Ghoubet wind farm guarantee
register.detail: MIGA · fiscal year 2019 · guarantee holder Djibouti Wind LP · term of up to 20 years
register.text: A MIGA guarantee of US$250 million, held by Djibouti Wind LP for a term of up to 20 years, for the 60-megawatt wind farm at Ghoubet; MIGA lists it as active. It supports private investment in a power plant that serves the energy standard.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 28.8% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Agricultural cooperative of Antar
items.text: A cooperative in Damerjog whose members received solar irrigation pumps, which allow production all year and cut losses after harvest; it has become a regular supplier to catering companies. Of the 40 beneficiaries supported, 70% are women, and sales rose by 50% and household income by 80%.

items.name: Agricultural cooperative of Dafenaytou
items.text: A cooperative of more than 70 members in northern Djibouti, most of them women, who hold half the seats on its board. With simple irrigation, resistant seeds and training from a regional climate project of IGAD funded by the African Development Bank’s Africa Climate Change Fund, members grow family vegetable gardens and forage plots, and a member reports a small surplus to sell.

items.name: Medyc
items.text: A Djiboutian e-health company, launched in 2019, that offers online consultations, home care and real-time glucose monitoring for people with diabetes, and delivers medicines and test strips to 300 to 500 patients. 1,200 people are registered on its online platform.

items.name: Caisse Populaire d’Épargne et de Crédit (CPEC)
items.text: A cooperative of solidarity finance, created in 2008, that offers savings and small loans to micro-enterprises and to people without access to banks, so that they can start income-generating activities. The World Bank Group strengthened the CPEC microfinance network in its programme for women’s and youth entrepreneurship, under which about 4,000 people, 55% of them women, gained access to financing from 2018 to March 2024.

items.name: Women’s agricultural cooperative of Guirori
items.text: A women’s cooperative in Guirori, in the Tadjourah region, that grows fodder for livestock on communal land it manages, with members sharing the benefits equally. In December 2025 an IGAD project set out to equip 30 of its beneficiaries, mostly women, with tools, drought-resistant seeds and training in sustainable fodder production.
